title: Phase 2: frontend-reach
hook: A frontend request in plain words now reaches the frontend surface: all 13 everyday probes route to `sk-code-frontend`, where 12 used to return `defer`. A review of a UI component loads the frontend standards beside the review mode, and none of the 8 look-alike prompts is pulled in.
recent: Routed plain frontend requests to the frontend surface and proved it with the 22 probes
what: You can ask for a sticky navbar, a dark mode toggle or a faster landing page and the hub loads the frontend references. Editing a `.css`, `.scss`, `.html`, `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.vue` or `.svelte` file now detects the `FRONTEND` surface ahead of `SKILLED`. The four bare keywords that matched unrelated sentences (`hover`, `padding`, `animation`, `easing`) are gone, and every frontend keyword is a phrase. Three playbook scenarios, `RD-003` to `RD-005`, hold the result.
files: `FRONTEND` detection block, and aliases equal to the `code-frontend-aliases` class
46 added phrases, 4 single words removed, new `code-frontend-review` class
`INTENT_SIGNALS` rows mirror the 162 phrases, and two sentences corrected
The statement that detection never selects the frontend surface is corrected in every copy
Three scenario files and their root index rows
Three expectations that encoded a hub with no specific surface
Policy hash after the vocabulary change
how: The vocabulary was designed against a replay of the router's own matching rule, then each edit went to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at max thinking through cli-pi as one literal brief: 15 dispatches, each diff read before the next. The orchestrating session ran the manifest refresh, the generator the pre-commit gate named, the probe replay, the baseline comparison, the three affected test suites, the drift guards and the quality runner. The code landed as `40b8d7e6b7`.
decisions: The review bundle rests on one frontend phrase per review prompt
The router bundles two modes only on an equal score, so `accessibility issues` matches the review probe and `react component` was left out on purpose
`lazy loading` and `grid layout` were left out
A replay showed both match non-frontend prompts such as lazy loading of Python modules
Three test expectations changed, one of them outside `.skilled/skills/sk-code/`

Each test asserted that the hub has no specific surface, which the planned `FRONTEND` block ends. Leaving them red would have made the in-scope change incorrect. Parent decision D5 names files outside sk-code, so the operator is asked to confirm the one line in `.skilled/bin/tests/compiled-route-surface-hint.test.cjs`
The prose keyword list in `sk-code-frontend/ROUTER.md` section 2 was not extended
Phase 004 replaces that section with a pointer to the machine block
The manifest was refreshed with `compiled-route-manifest.cjs refresh`
`tasks.md` names `compiled-route-sync.cjs`, but that command checks the served engine copies. The stale artifact was the activation manifest, and the guard printed the refresh command
verify: First target of every baseline route to a non-frontend packet
`node --test` on the sk-code-skilled tests, the sk-code-quality tests and `compiled-route-surface-hint.test.cjs`
router-sync, doc-claims and stack-folders PASS. alignment-drift fails on the same 23 files as the baseline
`sk-code` is the top hub for each
limits:
1. **A review bundle needs an exact score tie.** A review prompt that matches two frontend phrases routes to the frontend surface alone. `RD-004` holds the probe, and its triage says which phrase to remove.
2. **`.tsx` now detects FRONTEND first.** A TypeScript component under `.skilled/` reports `FRONTEND` then `SKILLED`. The operator chose `.tsx` and `.jsx` as frontend markers.
3. **The setup battery still ends `STATUS=FAIL`.** Its drift guard fails on 23 files outside sk-code, which phase 005 owns.
